almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

arcturus.title: Arcturus
arcturus.note: The King James rendering of a Hebrew word in Job. It most likely means the Great Bear, not the star we now call Arcturus.

barachel.title: Barachel
barachel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
barachel.note: Barachel the Buzite was Elihu's father, and Elihu was the youngest of those who spoke to Job.

behemoth.title: Behemoth
behemoth.note: The huge land animal God points Job to as proof of his own power. Most read the description as a hippopotamus.

bildad.title: Bildad
bildad.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
bildad.note: The second of Job's three friends to speak, a Shuhite. Like the others he insisted that Job's suffering had to come from hidden sin, and God later rebukes them for it.

buzite.title: Buzite
buzite.note: Elihu, the younger man whose speeches close the dialogue in Job, was a Buzite: of the family of Ram, from the kindred of Buz. Buz was a son of Nahor and brother of Uz.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

elihu.title: Elihu
elihu.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
elihu.note: The younger man in Job who waits until everyone else has finished and then speaks last. He faults Job for justifying himself and the three older friends for never actually answering him. Then God speaks from the whirlwind.

eliphaz-2.title: Eliphaz
eliphaz-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eliphaz-2.note: First and apparently oldest of Job's three friends, a Temanite. His speeches say suffering always comes from your own sin. At the end God rebukes him for not speaking rightly, as Job had.

jemimah.title: Jemimah
jemimah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
jemimah.note: The eldest of Job's daughters, born after God restored him, and her father gave his daughters an inheritance alongside their brothers, which the Old Testament rarely says of anyone.

jetheth.title: Jetheth
jetheth.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetheth.note: Edom had clan chiefs who came down from Esau, and Jetheth is listed with them.

job.title: Job
job.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
job.note: Uz was his country, and he was rich and righteous until God let Satan take his children, his wealth and his health to see whether his faith was only about the good life. He never curses God, but he does demand an answer. When God speaks from the whirlwind he gives no reason, only the size of creation, and Job goes quiet and gets back double.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

keren-happuch.title: Keren-happuch
keren-happuch.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
keren-happuch.note: Job's youngest daughter, born after God restored him. Her name means "horn of eye paint." She and her sisters got an inheritance alongside their brothers, which was unusual.

kezia.title: Kezia
kezia.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
kezia.note: The second of Job's three daughters, born after God restored him, and given an inheritance with her brothers.

naamathite.title: Naamathite
naamathite.note: The tag on Zophar, one of Job's three friends. Naamah, wherever it was, may have been in Arabia.

ophir.title: Ophir
ophir.note: It was the gold that made Ophir famous across the ancient world. Solomon's ships, sailing with Hiram of Tyre, brought it back in quantity, and the place itself was likely in southern Arabia or along the Red Sea.

rahab-2.title: Rahab
rahab-2.note: Not the woman from Jericho. This Rahab is the sea monster the poets use for chaos, and by extension a nickname thrown at Egypt.

ram-3.title: Ram
ram-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ram-3.note: One of 3 men called Ram. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named once in Job.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

sheba-3.title: Sheba
sheba-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sheba-3.note: A name among the nations in Genesis 10:7 and 1 Chronicles 1:9. Job 1:15 has raiders from Sheba carrying off Job's oxen and killing his servants.

shiphi.title: Shiphi
shiphi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shiphi.note: A Simeonite, father of Ziza. In Hezekiah's reign the tribe was pushing out into new pasture near Gedor, and Ziza was one of its leaders.

shuhite.title: Shuhite
shuhite.note: Bildad, one of Job's three friends, was a Shuhite. The word probably makes him a descendant of Shuah, Abraham's son by Keturah, whose people lived out in the Arabian desert.

tema.title: Tema
tema.note: An oasis in the north Arabian desert, on the caravan road between Damascus and the Arabian interior, named for a son of Ishmael. Job's friend Eliphaz compares Job's useless helpers to the caravans of Tema. Much later the Babylonian king Nabonidus made it his residence.

temani.title: Temani
temani.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
temani.note: Teman was Esau's grandson, and his Edomite clan had a name for wisdom. This is the word for that clan, and it is what Eliphaz is called all through Job.

uz.title: Uz
uz.note: Job lived in the land of Uz. Where it was is uncertain, somewhere east of Israel, perhaps in Edom.

zophar.title: Zophar
zophar.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zophar.note: The Naamathite, the third of Job's friends and the bluntest. He insisted Job's suffering proved hidden sin. God rebuked him for it.
